0x00437290 SHIPMOVE::Update_Ship_ETAs_

fail

- Parameter type does not match: assembly compares `param_1` as a 16-bit value (`CMP AX, [ESP+param_1]`), but the project declares/defines `int32_t player_id`. This is not cosmetic because callers and signedness/width are part of validation.
  Suggested diff:
  ```cpp
  - void __cdecl Update_Ship_ETAs_(int32_t player_id);
  + void __cdecl Update_Ship_ETAs_(int16_t player_id);
  ```

- The implementation introduces unnecessary 32-bit widening for the destination coordinates and loop comparisons. Assembly keeps the star coordinates and current coordinates as 16-bit locals and uses signed 16-bit loads with `MOVSX` only at compare/call boundaries. This is a likely type restoration issue and should remain in 16-bit space except where C promotion naturally occurs.
  Suggested diff:
  ```cpp
  - int32_t target_x = (int32_t)star->x;
  - int32_t target_y = (int32_t)star->y;
  + int16_t target_x = star->x;
  + int16_t target_y = star->y;

  - while ((int32_t)current_x != target_x || (int32_t)current_y != target_y) {
  + while (current_x != target_x || current_y != target_y) {
  ```

- Owner argument handling is too loosely typed at the call site. Assembly does `MOVSX AX, byte ptr [ESI+0x63]` then pushes that value; the source forces `(uint8_t)ship->owner`. Since `owner` is signed `char` in the recovered type info, this cast changes semantics for negative owners and does not match the recovered calling sequence.
  Suggested diff:
  ```cpp
  - GEO::Move_Player_1_Turn_To_Star_((uint8_t)ship->owner, ...)
  + GEO::Move_Player_1_Turn_To_Star_(ship->owner, ...)
  ```
  If the callee prototype is truly `uint8_t`, this needs broader signature/type reconciliation with the original binary before validation can pass.

0x00444FA0 AIDUDES::Do_Blockaded_Colony_

fail

- Uses the wrong qsort comparator. Assembly calls `AIDUDES::Sort_Pops_FI_` at `0x445320`, but the implementation calls `Sort_Pops_FR_I_`. This changes ordering and downstream assignment behavior.
  ```diff
  -        qsort(&colony->pop[(uint8_t)colony_info->first_assignable_pop_idx],
  -              (uint8_t)colony->n_pops - (uint8_t)colony_info->first_assignable_pop_idx,
  -              4,
  -              Sort_Pops_FR_I_);
  +        qsort(&colony->pop[(uint8_t)colony_info->first_assignable_pop_idx],
  +              (uint8_t)colony->n_pops - (uint8_t)colony_info->first_assignable_pop_idx,
  +              4,
  +              Sort_Pops_FI_);
  ```

- In the `food2_per_farmer == 0` path, the job-bit update is not equivalent to the XOR-mask sequence from assembly. The binary toggles bits `0x80/0x100` via `((x ^ mask) & 0x180) ^ x`, preserving whichever target bit is selected from `Event_Check_Colony_Researching_`; current code forcibly clears `0x80` and ORs one mask. That can differ if source state is unexpected or mixed.
  ```diff
  -                colony->pop[(uint8_t)colony_info->cur_pop_idx] = (colony->pop[(uint8_t)colony_info->cur_pop_idx] & 0xFFFFFE7F) | job_mask;
  +                uint32_t& pop = colony->pop[(uint8_t)colony_info->cur_pop_idx];
  +                pop = ((pop ^ job_mask) & 0x180) ^ pop;
  ```

- The parameter type passed to `Event_Check_Colony_Researching_` is broadened unnecessarily: assembly zero-extends the byte colony index to 32-bit before push; current code casts to `uint16_t`. Likely harmless at runtime, but it is not the precise source-level match and suggests type drift.
  ```diff

  +            int16_t is_researching = EVENTS::Event_Check_Colony_Researching_((int)(uint8_t)colony_info->colony_idx);
  ```

00444E80 AIDUDES::Colony_AI_Given_Tax_

fail

- `_n_our_blockaded` and `_n_our_unblockaded` are typed incorrectly in the project as `uint16_t`, but the assembly uses `MOVSX` and `JLE`, so both counts are signed 16-bit values. This affects exact control-flow semantics for negative values and signed comparisons.
  Suggested diff:
  ```diff
  - inline uint16_t& _n_our_blockaded = *reinterpret_cast<uint16_t*>(std::uintptr_t{0x005657C0});
  - inline uint16_t& _n_our_unblockaded = *reinterpret_cast<uint16_t*>(std::uintptr_t{0x005657C4});
  + inline int16_t& _n_our_blockaded = *reinterpret_cast<int16_t*>(std::uintptr_t{0x005657C0});
  + inline int16_t& _n_our_unblockaded = *reinterpret_cast<int16_t*>(std::uintptr_t{0x005657C4});
  ```

- Because of the wrong unsigned typing, the two `for` loops in `Colony_AI_Given_Tax_` do not preserve the original signed termination behavior. In the binary, a negative count causes the loop to be skipped due to end-pointer comparison; in the current code, a negative signed memory value reinterpreted as `uint16_t` becomes a huge positive bound.
  Suggested diff:
  ```diff
  - for (int i = 0; i < aidudes::_n_our_blockaded; ++i) {
  + for (int i = 0; i < (int)aidudes::_n_our_blockaded; ++i) {
        aidudes::Do_Blockaded_Colony_(&aidudes::_our_blockaded[i]);
    }

  - for (int i = 0; i < aidudes::_n_our_unblockaded; ++i) {
  + for (int i = 0; i < (int)aidudes::_n_our_unblockaded; ++i) {
        aidudes::Do_Unblockaded_Colony_(&aidudes::_our_unblockaded[i]);
    }
  ```
  But this only becomes correct once the globals are retyped signed.

- The final condition also depends on signedness. The assembly does `CMP word ptr [...],0` followed by `JLE`, i.e. signed `<= 0`. With the current unsigned global type, `if (_n_our_unblockaded > 0)` is not equivalent for negative stored values.
  Suggested diff:
  ```diff
  - if (aidudes::_n_our_unblockaded > 0) {
  + if (aidudes::_n_our_unblockaded > 0) {
        aidudes::Assign_Additional_Unblockaded_Farmers_();
    } else {
        COLCALC::Do_Player_Colony_Post_Production_(aidudes::_i_ai);
    }
  ```
  The source text stays the same, but only after changing `_n_our_unblockaded` to `int16_t` does it match the binary.

0x00440340 OFFICER::Print_Galmap_Scanned_Ship_

fail

- Owner signedness is wrong. The binary uses `MOVSX` from `ship->owner`, so comparisons and argument passing are signed 8-bit semantics. Current code forces `uint8_t`, changing behavior for values >= 0x80.
- `SYS::N_Ships_By_Type_At_Location_` arguments are swapped versus the call site in assembly. The binary passes pointers in order: total, colony_ships, outposts/bases, transports, hull_counts. Current prototype/use is total, bases, colony_ships, transports, causing `n_outposts` and `n_colony_ships` text to be reversed here.
- The stack-owner/race-name branch condition is off by one. Assembly uses `CMP DI,0x8` / `JLE`, so fallback stack-owner lookup happens only when owner > 8. Current code is correct in branch shape after unsigned cast removal, but with the present unsigned cast it can misroute negative special owners into player-color/race paths incorrectly. This is a correctness risk tied to the same signedness bug above.
- Local buffer/layout behavior does not match the binary exactly for the “named stack” path. Assembly copies the uppercased race name into a second buffer before printing (`local_21c`), while current code prints `race_name` directly. This may be harmless in practice, but because this function uses overlapping fixed stack regions in the original, I cannot confirm exact aliasing/temporary behavior from the restored source as-is.

  ```diff
  -       }
  -       break;
  ```

  ```diff
  +     if (right_limit > x2_ex) {
  +         right_limit = x2_ex;
  +     }
  + } else if (right_limit <= x2_ex && excl_right_x > x2_ex) {
  +     excl_right_x = x2_ex;
  ```

  and similarly for the `x1_ex` half:

0x0041FFA0 BEAMS::Rob_Interpolate_Line_

fail

Discrepancies:
- The binary uses a very specific signed halving / bisection algorithm with truncation semantics derived from `cdq; sub eax,edx; sar eax,1`, but the current code uses plain C++ `/ 2` on potentially negative values. That does not match instruction-for-instruction for odd negative deltas and can shift the interpolation point by 1.
  Suggested diff snippet:
  ```cpp
  static int32_t half_toward_zero_asm(int32_t v) {
      return (v - (v >> 31)) >> 1;
  }

  // then replace:
  cur_x += (high_x - cur_x) / 2;
  cur_y += (high_y - cur_y) / 2;
  cur_x += (low_x - cur_x) / 2;
  cur_y += (low_y - cur_y) / 2;

  // with:
  cur_x += half_toward_zero_asm(high_x - cur_x);
  cur_y += half_toward_zero_asm(high_y - cur_y);
  cur_x += half_toward_zero_asm(low_x - cur_x);
  cur_y += half_toward_zero_asm(low_y - cur_y);
  ```

- The current midpoint initialization `dx / 2` and `dy / 2` also does not reproduce the assembly’s `sar` behavior for negative odd values. The binary uses arithmetic right shift, not signed division.
  Suggested diff snippet:
  ```cpp
  int32_t cur_x = dx >> 1;
  int32_t cur_y = dy >> 1;
  ```

- The current implementation relies on `abs(...)` from C++, while the assembly computes absolute value manually in 32-bit signed arithmetic. This is usually equivalent here, but for strict restoration/validation it introduces avoidable semantic uncertainty, especially around exact signed behavior.
  Suggested diff snippet:
  ```cpp
  static int32_t abs32_asm(int32_t v) {
      int32_t s = v >> 31;
      return (v ^ s) - s;
  }

  int32_t max_dist = abs32_asm(dx);
  if (abs32_asm(dy) > max_dist) max_dist = abs32_asm(dy);
  ...
  int32_t cur_dist = abs32_asm(cur_x);
  if (abs32_asm(cur_y) > cur_dist) cur_dist = abs32_asm(cur_y);
  ```

0x0042C350 INVASION::Change_Pop_Ownership_

  and likewise for building `31`.

- `new_owner` is declared `uint32_t`, but the binary uses it as an 8-bit player id in byte stores/bitfield updates and as a scaled player index expected in range 0..7. This type mismatch hides required truncation semantics and can affect comparisons/bit packing in the pop loop.

  ```cpp
      break;
  ```

This is observably wrong for `target_type != 0` missile targets, where the assembly path for case `0x21` does not touch `_combat_data[target_idx].shield_type` or `.size_class`.

  ```cpp
          ...
          break;
      case 0x23:
      case 0x24:

          ...
          break;
      }
      case 0x0D:

          int size_mult = MOX::_combat_data[target_idx].size_class + 1;
          ...
          break;
      }
  }
  ```

The binary sign-extends `count`, `shots_left`, `arc`, `type`, `min_damage`, `max_damage`, `size_class`, and `shield_type`-derived values from packed byte/word fields. 0044f640 CMBTAI::Average_Missile_Kills_

- Return type/signature mismatch: assembly returns `AX`/`short`; project declares and defines `int32_t`. This is not cosmetic because caller expectations and promotion behavior differ from the original ABI.
  ```diff
  - int32_t __cdecl Average_Missile_Kills_(int16_t ship_idx, int16_t weapon_slot_idx, int16_t msl_count, int16_t msl_type, int16_t* remaining_pd_count, int16_t param6);
  + int16_t __cdecl Average_Missile_Kills_(int16_t ship_idx, int16_t weapon_slot_idx, int16_t msl_count, int16_t msl_type, int16_t* remaining_pd_count, int16_t param6);
  ```

- Comparison against `param6` is wrong in source. Assembly does `CMP AX,0xFFFF / JLE`, i.e. signed `param6 <= -1` selects fixed range `2`; otherwise it calls `Range_To_Missile_`. Current code uses `if (param6 > -1)` which is logically equivalent, but the decompiler input says `if (param_6 < 0)` and the real assembly behavior is specifically `<= -1`. This is acceptable logically; no issue by itself. The actual discrepancy is elsewhere below.

- Point-defense remaining count update is reversed at the end. Assembly:
  - computes `kills = current_health / divisor`
  - if `param_3 < kills`, stores `current_health - param_3 * divisor`, returns `param_3`
  - else stores `0`, returns `kills`
  
  Current code does:
  ```cpp
  kills = current_health / divisor;
  if (msl_count < kills) {
      *remaining_pd_count = current_health - (msl_count * divisor);
      return msl_count;
  } else {
      *remaining_pd_count = 0;
  }
  ```
  This condition is correct, but the function returns `int32_t`, not `int16_t`, and more importantly the local/temporary typing around `current_health`, `divisor`, and `kills` is not constrained to the original 16-bit behavior. The binary performs 16-bit signed division and stores in 16-bit registers throughout (`DI`, `BX`, `SI`, `AX`), so overflow/truncation semantics matter.

  Minimal correction:
  ```diff
  - int32_t __cdecl Average_Missile_Kills_(...)
  + int16_t __cdecl Average_Missile_Kills_(...)
  ```

- `base_dmg` is typed as `int32_t`, but assembly keeps this value in `BP` as a 16-bit quantity after `IMUL BP,BP,0x5` and subsequent 16-bit add. Using wider arithmetic can hide original signed wrap/truncation behavior.
  ```diff

  + int16_t base_dmg = (int16_t)((TECHDATA::_weapons[slot_weapon_id].min_damage + TECHDATA::_weapons[slot_weapon_id].max_damage) * 5);
  ```

- `current_health` is read from `*remaining_pd_count` as `int16_t`, but subsequent arithmetic uses mixed-width C expressions instead of preserving the binary’s 16-bit signed semantics around `IDIV BX`. This needs explicit 16-bit locals/return type to match original behavior precisely.
  ```diff
  - int16_t current_health = *remaining_pd_count;
  - int16_t divisor;
  - kills = current_health / divisor;
  + int16_t current_health = *remaining_pd_count;
  + int16_t divisor;
  + int16_t kills = current_health / divisor;
  ```

- `Turn_Cost_` path computes turn amount incorrectly for negative deltas. Assembly uses signed-abs/sign-restoration on `(new_facing - old_facing + 16) & 0xf`, not plain `% 16`. Current code:

0048DB60 SCROLL::Scroll_Down_One_Item_

fail

- `row_step` signedness is not validated correctly in the implementation. The assembly does `MOV CL, [ESI+1A]` followed by `AND ECX, 0xffff00ff`, which preserves only the low 8 bits and makes the effective step an unsigned byte value in `CX`. The current code uses `uint16_t step = (uint16_t)sb->row_step;`, which first converts from signed `int8_t` and can sign-extend negative values before widening. This changes behavior for values >= 0x80.
  Suggested diff snippet:
  ```cpp
  uint8_t step = (uint8_t)sb->row_step;
  sb->first_visible_row += step;
  ...
  sb->thumb_center_y -= (sb->track_len_px / sb->total_rows) * step;
  ```

- The bottom-clamp branch uses `sb->thumb_height_px / 2`, which in C++ on signed integers rounds toward zero. The assembly sequence `MOVSX EAX, word ptr [ESI+6] / CDQ / SUB EAX, EDX / SAR EAX,1` implements signed divide-by-2 with floor semantics, not truncation toward zero. This differs for negative odd `thumb_height_px`.
  Suggested diff snippet:
  ```cpp
  int16_t half_height = (int16_t)(((int32_t)sb->thumb_height_px - ((int32_t)sb->thumb_height_px >> 31)) >> 1);
  sb->thumb_center_y = half_height;
  ```

- The function currently relies on high-level arithmetic promotions for `first_visible_row += step`; the assembly explicitly performs 16-bit addition (`ADD AX,CX`) and stores back to the 16-bit field before sign-extending for the comparison. If exact overflow/wrap behavior matters, this should be expressed more explicitly to match the binary.
  Suggested diff snippet:
  ```cpp
  sb->first_visible_row = (int16_t)((uint16_t)sb->first_visible_row + (uint8_t)sb->row_step);
  ```

Given the project’s restoration precision requirements, this is not strict enough to validate from source alone.

  Minimal suggested diff snippet:

The current code expresses this as `if (dist >= dist_sq)`, but names the threshold as `dist_sq` and the local as `dist`, which suggests squared-distance semantics rather than generic signed integer comparison from the original. Although likely equivalent, this loses precision required for validation of exact early-exit behavior.


Current code stores `n_pops` in `int8_t` and uses `(int16_t)n_pops` as the upper bound, which becomes negative for values >= 0x80 and changes control flow.
  Suggested diff snippet:
  ```cpp
  bool __cdecl Colony_Has_Natives_(int16_t colony_idx) {
      uint8_t n_pops = (uint8_t)MOX::_colony[colony_idx].n_pops;

      if (n_pops != 0) {
          for (int16_t i = 0; i < (int16_t)n_pops; ++i) {
              if ((MOX::_colony[colony_idx].pop[i] & 0x0F) == 8) {
                  return true;
              }
          }
      }
      return false;
  }
  ```

- Local type choice obscures the actual binary behavior. The disassembly starts with `DX = 0`, uses `DX` as the loop counter, and repeatedly reloads `CL` from `n_pops`; the comparison semantics are unsigned-count driven, not signed `int8_t` driven. This should be reflected explicitly to avoid accidental miscompilation or future “cleanup” into signed logic.

004E9780 MAINMENU::Draw_Credits_

fail

- Fade-in line selection is off by one at the threshold. Assembly uses `JG 0xB3`, so the fade-in path is taken only when `_credit_y <= 0xB3`. Current code uses `< 0xB3`, which excludes `_credit_y == 0xB3`.
  ```diff
  - if (MAINMENU::_credit_y < 0xB3 /* 179 */) {
  + if (MAINMENU::_credit_y <= 0xB3 /* 179 */) {
        fade_in_line_idx = (int16_t)((0xB3 - MAINMENU::_credit_y) / 14);
    }
  ```

- The fade-in step computation does not match the signed 16-bit division sequence in assembly. The binary computes `((_credit_y - 0xB3) % 14) / 3`, with signed truncation via `CWD/IDIV`, then doubles the quotient. Current code stores the remainder in `int16_t` and does `remainder / 3`, which is close but still relies on C `%` behavior and misses the explicit 16-bit signed path the assembly uses. This is not precise enough for validation.
  ```diff
  - int16_t remainder = (MAINMENU::_credit_y - 0xB3) % 14;
  - int8_t step = (int8_t)((remainder / 3) * 2);
  + int16_t delta = (int16_t)(MAINMENU::_credit_y - 0xB3);
  + int16_t remainder = (int16_t)(delta % 14);
  + int8_t step = (int8_t)(((int16_t)(remainder / 3)) * 2);
  ```

- The final reset condition is expressed as `abs(_credit_y - 179) > _max_credits * 14`, but the assembly does a branchless signed absolute-value transform on 32-bit `EAX` after loading `_credit_y` from memory and comparing against `(_max_credits * 14)` computed as `((n * 8) - n) * 2`. While algebraically similar, using `abs()` introduces library semantics and potential edge-case ambiguity not present in the original instruction sequence. For strict restoration validation, this should be spelled in integer arithmetic mirroring the binary.
  ```diff
  - if (abs(MAINMENU::_credit_y - 179) > MAINMENU::_max_credits * 14) {
  + int32_t delta = (int32_t)MAINMENU::_credit_y - 0xB3;
  + int32_t mag = (delta < 0) ? -delta : delta;
  + if (mag > (int32_t)MAINMENU::_max_credits * 14) {
        MAINMENU::_credit_x = 0x42 /* 66 */;
        MAINMENU::_credit_y = 0x1A6 /* 422 */;
        MAINMENU::_delay_count = 10;
    }
  ```

004FD9C0 CMBTMIS::Coord_Movement_

- The current implementation adds behavior not present in the binary: it guards `dx != 0` and writes `*out_y = 0` in that case. The assembly performs an unconditional `IDIV EDI` in the `abs_dx >= abs_dy` branch, so if `dx == 0` there is no safety fallback; the restored source must not change that control flow.
- Parameter typing is too wide for `step`. The binary reads only `byte ptr [ESP + param_5]`, masks to 8 bits, and multiplies signed `±1` by that zero-extended byte. The current signature and implementation use `int16_t step`, which can incorrectly preserve high bits if callers ever pass values outside 0..255.
- The current code’s explicit casts and comments suggest a different semantic model than the actual instruction behavior; the binary specifically does 16-bit signed multiply for `AX * CX(low16)` after zero-extending the input byte into `CL`, then sign-extends the 16-bit result for the proportional division.

```cpp
if (abs_dx < abs_dy) {
    int16_t sy = (dy < 0) ? -1 : 1;
    int16_t v = (int16_t)(sy * step);
    *out_y = v;
    *out_x = (int16_t)((int32_t)v * dx / dy);
} else {
```

Discrepancies:
- Character bounds check uses unsigned semantics in current code, but assembly uses signed compare after `MOVSX`/`JG`.
  - Assembly accepts all signed char values `<= 0x80`, including negative chars; current code rejects any byte value `> 128`, so bytes `0x81..0xFF` are incorrectly rejected instead of being sign-extended and passed through.
  - Minimal suggested diff:
    ```cpp
    -    if ((uint8_t)ch > 128) {
    +    if (ch > 0x80) {
             return;
         }
    ```

- Width lookup index uses zero-extension in current code, but assembly uses sign-extended index.
  - `MOVSX EAX,AX` then `MOVSX SI,byte ptr [EAX + _font_header.font_style_widths]` means negative `char` values index before `font_style_widths[0]`. Current code forces `(uint8_t)ch`, which changes memory access behavior for negative chars.
  - Minimal suggested diff:
    ```cpp
    -    short glyph_w = (short)_font_header.font_style_widths[(uint8_t)ch];
    +    short glyph_w = (short)_font_header.font_style_widths[(int16_t)ch];
    ```

- Height clipping lacks the original non-positive-height guard.
  - Assembly can produce `DI = ((anim_h - 1) - draw_y) + 1` and still call the callee even if zero/negative after vertical clipping; however if `draw_y` starts negative there is no early return. More importantly, the current code never checks whether the final clipped height became non-positive before the call, relying on callee behavior. This is ambiguous against the exact control flow and should be reviewed together with the callee contract.
  - Minimal suggested diff if matching caller-side clipping strictly is desired:
    ```cpp
         short clipped_h = font_h;
         if ((int)draw_y + (int)clipped_h > (int)max_y_idx) {
             clipped_h = max_y_idx - draw_y + 1;
         }
    +    if (clipped_h < 1) {
    +        return;
    +    }
    ```

Main blocking issue is the signedness mismatch on `ch`, which changes both branch behavior and memory accesses, so validation cannot pass.

The assembly iterates contiguous dwords from `DAT_0058d7a8` up to but not including `arith1e::_code` at `0x0058DBAC`, i.e. exactly the `totals` table in memory. In source, `totals` is declared as `int* totals[END_OF_STREAM];` followed by `uint16_t code;`; this is plausible, but the explicit nulling means the generated code cannot match the shown instruction sequence.

Minimal suggested diff snippet:
```cpp
static void __cdecl uninit_model_() {
    for (int context = 0; context < END_OF_STREAM; context++) {
        free(totals[context]);
    }
}
```
